How does taking care of a lizard work? I've never owned one, but they always seemed like really chill pets haha.

Well, once to get them set up, they're pretty easy to care for. They just require a little bit of work and you'll spend a lot of money getting them what they need to be happy and healthy for years to come. I'll give you a quick rundown of basics.

  • You need two heat lamps. Usually. One for UVA and one for UVB. The UVA bulb is the cheaper bulb and is there to provide heat and help your reptile see. The UVB bulb is the one that is more expensive. We're talking at least $20-$25 American if you get one of the lower-end bulbs. They can cost up to $60 and need replaced every year as the bulb starts to have a decreased ability to produce UVB light over time. If you're willing, you can buy a single bulb that has both UVA and UVB combined into one bulb, but they are generally more expensive and most people are not willing to dish out that much money.
  • The UVB light is very, very, very important for your reptile's physical health. Without UVB rays, your reptile will be unable to process calcium properly and what happens is that your reptile starts having a weakened bone structure. This is bad and leads to Metabolic Bone Disease. (WARNING: NOT SAFE FOR LIFE) Mild cases can be treated and generally won't affect the life of the reptile. More severe (like linked) is from severe neglect and will affect their life.
  • You need to balance their diet. Different lizards and reptiles have different eating habits and nutritional needs. Always look up and research diet. Sometimes, they can be stubborn and won't eat what they need. My gecko is an insectivore and is great about eating what she needs. On the other hand, my dragon is an omnivore, but seems to be a bit of a special case. He won't eat any types of fruit or vegetables unless it is dried and he seems to really like pellets that have a general idea of what they need nutritional wise. He only likes them in certain colors. He is very odd.
  • Iceberg lettuce has no nutritional value.
  • Reptiles love live insects.
  • Don't use loose substrate (flooring) for your reptiles. They can be kind of dumb or clumsy and end up eating sand. This can lead to impaction, which is a general cloggage in their digestive system.
  • A 40 gallon tank is great for a Beardie and a 20 is perfect for a Gecko.
  • Leopard Geckos need a "hide" that has high humidity. It's like a little cave that has moist paper towels. They absorb moisture through their skin. So this is important.
  • My Bearded Dragon drinks water out of a water bowl. He gets his moisture through this and his baths that I give him every few days.

 

That's a basic gist. I probably forgot something but I just woke up and I'm trying to keep this general and not too long.

They are not chill all the time, but they are definitely neat little critters. My Gecko isn't too fond of being held, so when I let her out, I usually let her explore and do her thing in a big area where she can't hurt herself. (She decided to jump from my chest once and was lucky to not break anything) She seems to think she is a cat and will chase lazer pointers, play with tiny little stuffed animals, and will bite... anything. The Dragon is the more calm one. He really doesn't care where he is as long as he is around me. He seems to like my hair and fleece blanket and robe a lot when he isn't on my chest. There have been quite a few times where I thought he was behind my computer monitor and he actually was hidden in the blankets in my bed. It's very interesting being exhausted, climbing into bed, and wondering wtf is stabbing you when you throw your blanket over you! Oh yeah. He also likes to climb up onto my shoulder and smack or lick my face whenever he isn't getting enough attention.

Whoa, thanks for the thorough reply! I had no idea that reptiles needed very specific conditions -- it's kinda amazing lol.

I'm laughing at the idea of them being dumb or clumsy and tripping over themselves, even though it would be really bad if they swallowed sand as a result.

It's not a problem at all! I'd rather see someone educated, rather than be uneducated on them. Anything I can do to make having a reptile easier, I generally try to do. Makes it better for owner and pet and you'll enjoy your friend more.

When they're younger, they're definitely really clumsy. It can be really amusing! My Dragon when he was under 12 inches kinda sucked at walking. Instead, he would just take off, 0 to 60. Well, one day, I have him on a desk that didn't really have much traction. He decides to take off. His little legs go flailing about, he finds traction, takes off. Well, he found my phone on the desk and ran straight into it. He flew over the phone and ended up sliding on his face for a foot or so. He just looked over at me like "You didn't see anything." It was like something out of a cartoon. As an adult, he just falls off of things. He thinks he is really good at climbing so when he scales me, he sometimes finds himself failing at life and somewhere in my lap or between my back and the chair. The Gecko is also really bad at falling. She tries to climb on the artificial plants I have in her tank, thinking that they can support her weight. Eh. Doesn't work out too well.

Yeah. The sand thing is not uncommon. They're pretty silly. Fun fact, if the sand is "edible" and made of Calcium, Leopard Geckos would likely eat it for fun. For some reason, they really like eating Calcium raw.

Soon I'll be flying from Sydney to London and I've never even been on a plane before, what tips do you guys have to survive a flight like this?
What tips do you have for very long flights? (24 hours)
Download some offline games that last a while, also download some offline music. Lot of it so you don't get bored.

Take a seat next to the corridor so you can walk a bit once in a while. Also try to do a bit of exercise every few hours. There are lots of things you can do while seated just to not get too stiff and prevent thrombosis. Also maybe take a book with you. There should be plenty of films on the plane so you shouln't be too bored. Try not to drink to much of alcohol on the plane. This will prevent good resting. And you want to sleep a lot after the first excitement has settled. Also be at the airport about 1,5 - 2 hrs earlier than check in requires you. You never know what might happen (traffic, etc) and like this your safe. The last thing you want is missing your flight!

I don't sleep on 24 hour flights. I'd rather get to my destination exhausted and then crash on my bed. So, during the trip, I usually eat, watch movies, listen to music, read books and talk with other passengers or fellow travellers. If you have any work to do, you could also do that. I usually stock up on about 20-30 movies for the return trips. Try http://agoodmovietowatch.com/ for some movies that weren't as popular as they should have been
Audio books are great to not feel bored.

Business class.. Failing that, get one of those neck support pillows, a good book and the best noise cancelling headphones you can afford. Plus make sure to drink heaps of water and carry gum for the decent. A few snickers bars will also tie you over between meals.
Take full advantage of free foods and drinks, dont sleep for a long time before entering the flight, bring a pillow, bring a book.
